slides.headline: ONE $33 UBER COST MORE THAN FOUR DRIVERLESS TESLA RIDES COMBINED, AND IT SMELLED.
slides.image_prompt: Elon Musk, wide-eyed shock, back seat of self-driving Tesla Model Y, empty driver seat dominating left side, car clearly autonomous. Blurred city road through windshield. Crimson Tesla glow. Gold afternoon light. Documentary style, natural texture.

slides.headline: HE TOOK FOUR FULLY DRIVERLESS TESLA RIDES IN ONE DAY. ZERO DRIVERS.
slides.body:
Not a press event. Not a safety driver riding along. Four separate Tesla Model Y trips across one afternoon, nobody behind the wheel in any of them.

The price changed that assumption

slides.headline: FOUR RIDES. 50 MINUTES. 8 MILES. $27.25 TOTAL.
slides.body:
Each one picked up and dropped off by a car with nobody behind the wheel. Your daily commute fits inside that **8-mile** window.

Then came the Uber.

slides.headline: $33 FOR ONE. $27 FOR FOUR.
slides.body: That one Uber lasted **20 minutes** and still cost more.

slides.headline: THE CAR WITH NO DRIVER BEAT THE HUMAN ON CLEANLINESS TOO
slides.body:
Cleanliness: the Uber smelled. The robot didn't have anyone inside to make it smell.

Then the per-ride number came in.

slides.headline: FOUR RIDES AVERAGED $6.81 EACH. THE UBER COST NEARLY 5X MORE PER RIDE.
slides.body:
Corporate pickups. Recurring routes. Client transfers.

Every Uber receipt on your company card now has a real competitor. Every route your team keeps booking the old way is a cost that already looks wrong

slides.headline: SAVE THIS: FOUR DRIVERLESS TESLA RIDES COST LESS THAN ONE SMELLY UBER
slides.body:
4 driverless Tesla rides: **$27.25** total
50 minutes and **8 miles** covered
1 Uber ride: **$33** including tip
The Uber smelled. The robots didn't.

Send this to the friend who just paid surge pricing

caption:
Tesla's driverless robotaxi just beat Uber on both price and smell. Swipe to see what four fully autonomous rides actually cost. 🚗

The belief that robotaxis were still too experimental for everyday use, four driverless Model Y rides covering 50 minutes and 8 miles for $27.25 combined, the single Uber that cost $33 including tip and smelled, the twist where one human-driven ride was more expensive than all four robot rides together, what this means for Uber drivers facing a real-world price comparison, and why businesses booking repeat routes should pay attention.

Self-driving taxis just cleared the test that matters most: everyday cost. Four autonomous trips covered more ground for less than one Uber with a driver. When the robot gets cheaper than the human, it stops being the backup.

Running a business? DM us 'AI' and we'll show you what this changes for yours.

Sources: Sawyer Merritt on X
